### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via MCPServerRuntime (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `391e25be331a53aee1b8a168e1e75f757a40296e` — the merge of head `689463fd78db407702ca6113b4b9b05984557811` into base `1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 391e25be331a53aee1b8a168e1e75f757a40296e && git checkout 391e25be331a53aee1b8a168e1e75f757a40296e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df 689463fd78db407702ca6113b4b9b05984557811 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df && git merge --no-ff 689463fd78db407702ca6113b4b9b05984557811

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-18T01:34Z

Head-sha: 689463fd78db407702ca6113b4b9b05984557811
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34995 (os-dev report 6966266996).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #34995`, base `main`, with `main` merged in at the head. Five paths, +256/-47:
- `stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `plugin.ts`, and a docblock in `mcp-server-runtime.ts`;
- the pin file;
- an `@objectstack/mcp` patch changeset.

Not governed. `plugin.ts` is where the resources' view is set, so the claim's "where the resources are registered" covers it. I read it the same way o3-E does.

**Clause-②: `no` holds under the seat's ruling.** `servedLocaleObjectView` is exported from `stdio-data-bridge.ts` only. `@objectstack/mcp`'s index does not re-export that module, so no published export is added. The resources keep the same fields. Only the language of the label and description values changes, so no field is added, removed or renamed.

**CI.** It was still running when I read it (21 pending, nothing failed). This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

**One routine, moved as is.** `defaultLocaleSources` and `inServedLocale` move from inside `createStdioDataBridge` to module scope. The body is unchanged: `translateMetaList`, with `metaRequestLocale(undefined, i18n)` as the locale, and a throwing i18n resolver treated as none. The bridge's own dataset translation now passes `deps.i18n` explicitly, the one call site the closure used to cover.

**The new wrapper.** `servedLocaleObjectView` localizes `listObjects` and `getObject` over the view it wraps. It registers its own declared read, so `readObjectWithDeclaration` returns the localized served object beside the untranslated declaration, which is read for `readonly` alone. The tools and the resources now read the same wrapper over the same caller view:
- **The tools.** `createStdioDataBridge` builds `localizedView = servedLocaleObjectView(servedView, …)`. `list_objects` and `describe_object` read it.
- **The resources.** `plugin.ts` wraps the view it hands `setRuntimeObjectView` the same way: over `callerObjectView` when a stdio principal exists, else the bare view, with the same `optionalService('i18n')` and protocol reads. That view is read only by the two object-resource builders (`bridgeResources`, the `objects()` closure), so nothing else is affected.

**The mask holds.** The translator rewrites text on the fields it is given and adds none. It is applied to the served object, never the declaration, so a masked field stays absent along with its translated text.

**The pins drive the real wiring.** The #34995 block boots `MCPServerPlugin` over a host, with `i18n` registered or not, and reads the two resources through an MCP client:
- under a zh-CN default, both resources equal `describe_object` and `list_objects`, label for label;
- a masked field is absent from the translated resources;
- with an `en` default and no entry, or no i18n service, the tools and the resources both serve the authored text.

The #34872 block still holds over the moved routine. The ablation turns the resource pin red.

**HTTP.** Streamable HTTP registers no resources, so it is out of scope by construction, as the changeset says.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. The stdio locale is still the i18n service's default, the workspace default. The stdio transport carries no request, so a per-caller locale cannot exist here. The tools and the resources now agree on that one locale, which is what the card asked. Not owed.

Next: o3-E lands once the three aggregates are green. No seat L2 is owed. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
